question.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+2} & ={2}^{x+3} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x+2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+3})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
x+2=\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+3}).
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x+2=(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2 & =(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x+2 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-2 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-2 \\ x & =\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-2}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$
